questions.stem: What is the energy density of the electric field in air at a point where the field strength is 3 × 10⁶ V m⁻¹?

Read the following statements about an electric dipole of moment p in a uniform electric field E.
A. Its potential energy is minimum when p is parallel to E.
B. The torque on it is maximum where its potential energy is minimum.
C. Its potential energy is zero when p is perpendicular to E, with the usual choice of zero.
D. The work done in turning it from θ₁ to θ₂ is pE(cos θ₁ − cos θ₂).
Which statements are correct?

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about Kirchhoff's rules.
A. They can be applied only to circuits in which every element obeys Ohm's law.
B. If a current calculated with them comes out negative, the assumed direction of that current was opposite to the actual direction.
C. The sign given to the emf of a cell in a loop equation depends on the direction in which the loop is traversed, not on the direction of current through the cell.
D. For a circuit with two unknown branch currents, two independent loop equations (with the junction rule already used) are sufficient.
Which of the statements are correct?

questions.unit: Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism
questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about a rectangular current loop in a uniform magnetic field.
A. The net force on the loop is zero for every orientation.
B. The torque depends on the area of the loop but not on its shape.
C. The loop is in stable equilibrium when its magnetic moment is parallel to the field.
D. The torque is maximum when the magnetic moment is parallel to the field.
Choose the correct option.

questions.stem: A material has a relative permeability of $0.99998$. What kind of magnetic material is it?

questions.stem: When a p-n junction is formed and reaches equilibrium with no external voltage applied, which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Only diffusion occurs, and it continues until all the holes have crossed to the n-side

options.label: B
options.text: Diffusion of majority carriers sets up a field that causes drift of minority carriers; at equilibrium the diffusion and drift currents are equal and opposite

options.label: C
options.text: Only drift occurs, because the barrier field exists before the junction is formed

options.label: D
options.text: A steady current flows from p to n through the junction even without a battery

questions.stem: How many diodes does a bridge rectifier use?

options.label: A
options.text: Two diodes, connected to the two ends of the secondary so that one conducts in each half-cycle

options.label: B
options.text: One diode, connected in series so that it conducts in only one half-cycle of the input

options.label: C
options.text: Three diodes, connected so that one conducts in the first half-cycle and two in the next

options.label: D
options.text: Four diodes, connected so that two of them conduct in each half-cycle

questions.stem: In the circuit symbol of a junction diode, what does the arrowhead indicate?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: It shows the direction of the reverse saturation current through the diode

options.label: C
options.text: It shows the direction of the electric field in the depletion region

options.label: D

questions.stem: When pure silicon is doped with phosphorus, what happens to its hole concentration (at the same temperature)?

options.label: A
options.text: It increases, because each phosphorus atom also creates a hole

options.label: B
options.text: It remains equal to nᵢ, because doping affects only electrons

options.label: C
options.text: It becomes exactly zero, because donor electrons fill every hole

options.label: D
options.text: It falls below nᵢ, because the extra electrons recombine with holes more often
